claim.pdf_says:
NOTE    The VALIDATE facility is an obsolete feature.

Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in this facility will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove it from the next revision.  [both paragraphs printed in the reduced NOTE typeface - measured cap height 27 px at 300 dpi vs 30 px for the adjacent normative body paragraph 'The VALIDATE statement invokes data validation...'; the same wording appears elsewhere in the standard folded inside one note, e.g. 'NOTE 1    The STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item (SBIDI) is an obsolete feature. Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in this facility will be reevaluated...']
claim.markdown_says:
NOTE    The VALIDATE facility is an obsolete feature.

Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in this facility will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove it from the next revision.  [second paragraph rendered as an ordinary body paragraph, styled identically to the normative text above it, with no NOTE marker or continuation indent]
claim.why_it_matters: The second paragraph is the continuation of the NOTE, i.e. informative text. Rendered as an unmarked body paragraph it reads as normative provision text, so a reader (or a tool mining the transcription for requirements) would treat an editorial statement about the next revision as a conformance requirement of 14.9.50.1. Notes are non-normative per ISO drafting rules.

verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED - formatting-only, and not page-810-specific.

1. TEXT IS WORD-FOR-WORD IDENTICAL. specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 32792-32794 carry 'NOTE    The VALIDATE facility is an obsolete feature.', a blank line, then 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in this facility will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove it from the next revision.' Nothing is missing, added, reordered, or relocated. No word of the source differs.

2. THE PDF ITSELF PRINTS THESE AS TWO SEPARATE, UNMARKED, FLUSH-LEFT PARAGRAPHS. I rendered p810 at 300 dpi and cropped the region. The 'Unlike other obsolete features' paragraph begins at the SAME left margin as the 'NOTE' line - there is no continuation indent in the PDF, and no repeated NOTE marker. The claim's markdown description ('no NOTE marker or continuation indent') is therefore equally true of the PDF; by contrasting it against the PDF the claim implies the PDF supplies structure it does not supply. That part of the claim misdescribes the source.

3. THE ONLY REAL DIFFERENCE IS FONT SIZE, WHICH MARKDOWN DOES NOT ENCODE ANYWHERE. Measuring ink-row extents on the 300 dpi render: normative body line 1 spans 40 px, the NOTE line spans 37 px, the continuation line spans 37 px. So the continuation IS set in the reduced NOTE face (the claim's typographic observation is correct, if slightly off in absolute numbers), and the sole device distinguishing note from provision on this page is a ~7% type reduction. A plain-text/markdown transcription has no representation for point size. This is precisely the excluded category: a formatting difference that changes no content.

4. THE CONVENTION IS GLOBAL, NOT A PAGE-810 DEFECT. Scanning the whole transcription: 304 NOTE paragraphs begin with a bare, unstyled 'NOTE' at column 0; exactly 1 uses a blockquote and 0 use emphasis. NOTEs are never typographically set off anywhere in this file - including the FIRST paragraph of this very note, which is also 'styled identically to the normative text above it' and is identified solely by the literal word 'NOTE'. Page 810 is transcribed exactly like the other 303. Marking only this one would introduce an inconsistency, not remove one.

5. THE TRANSCRIPTION IS DEMONSTRABLY FOLLOWING THE PDF'S OWN PARAGRAPHING, NOT INVENTING IT. The claim's own counter-example proves this: at line 9015 the SBIDI note, which the PDF prints folded into a single note, is transcribed as a single folded line ('NOTE 1    The STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item (SBIDI) is an obsolete feature. Unlike other obsolete features, ...'), while at lines 9002-9004, 13211-13213 and 45370-45372 - where the PDF splits it - the transcription splits it. The transcription mirrors each occurrence's printed layout faithfully. The variance is ISO's own inconsistent styling of the same boilerplate, not a transcription error.

6. THE MISREADING RISK IS NOT MATERIAL. The paragraph contains no conformance verb - no 'shall', no 'is required', no permission or prohibition. It reads 'it is intended that interest in this facility will be reevaluated during the next revision', with 'this facility' anaphorically bound to the immediately preceding NOTE line's subject. A requirements-mining tool keying on normative verbs extracts nothing from it, and a human reading it directly under a line beginning 'NOTE' has the antecedent in view.

No content discrepancy. Verdict: not real.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a discrepancy. The markdown reproduces the PDF's words, paragraph order and paragraph break exactly, and the PDF itself gives the continuation paragraph no NOTE marker and no continuation indent - it is flush left, identical in position to the 'NOTE' line. The single distinguishing device in the PDF is a reduced type size (measured 37 px ink extent for both NOTE paragraphs vs 40 px for the adjacent normative body line at 300 dpi), which markdown cannot express and does not express for any of the 304 NOTE paragraphs in the transcription. If the project ever wants notes machine-distinguishable, that is a global transcription-convention change (e.g. wrapping every NOTE and its continuation paragraphs in blockquotes), not a page-810 content fix.
